page: Amazon Web Services r8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 processors on the arm64 architecture. The server provides 192 dedicated physical cores running at 2.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, maintaining a direct 1:1 ratio between vCPUs and physical cores. It features a per-core cache layout with 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache, supported by 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 1,536.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The system contains no integrated GPUs and includes no local storage, relying entirely on network-attached volumes over a 50 Gbps baseline network link.

Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystems alongside moderate single-core speeds. The 192 physical cores achieve top-tier ratings in stress-ng multi-core testing (291,012.56) and Geekbench multi-core workloads (21,021.0), with high performance in parallel tasks like Clang software compilation and ray tracing. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 896.26 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 412.85 GB/sec, driving top-tier PassMark database operations and 357.86 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread metrics—including stress-ng single-core (1,648.39) and Geekbench single-core (1,668.0)—remain in the average tier.

Hardware tradeoffs center around architecture specialization, absence of attached disk, and sequential processing limitations. Without local NVMe drives, storage access is dependent on external block storage networks. In addition, single-threaded throughput limits performance on unparallelized tasks, and lack of dedicated GPU hardware yields weak performance in generative LLM token generation (2.73 tokens/sec on 70B models). However, the density of 192 discrete arm64 execution pipelines paired with high DDR5 memory bandwidth provides qualitative cost efficiency for highly concurrent, memory-heavy workloads that avoid hyperthreading contention.

Amazon Web Services r8g.metal-48xl fits enterprise in-memory databases such as Redis, large-scale caching platforms, high-throughput database operations, heavy parallel code compilation, and distributed data processing pipelines.
